newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagrebacka Banka hits high in thin Croatian trade.
newsitem.headline: Zagrebacka Banka hits high in thin Croatian trade.

text.p: Zagrebacka Banka hit an all-time high on the Croatian stock market on Wednesday in very thin overall trade, with blue chips seen as the only likely candidates to break a pre-election lull.

Croatia votes in nation-wide municipal elections on April 13 and most traders predict the market will stagnate in anticipation of the results which are likely to loosen the ruling party's grip on power.
"Podravka was the only stock today with demand overshooting offers," said Josko Milisa of I.C.F. brokerage, adding the price of the food concern was likely to rise.
Podravka's shares gained 10 kuna to 310, on the day's record volume of 2,825 shares.
Six of 14 active issues fell, four rose and four were flat. Volume halved to 5,966 shares while turnover slumped to a mere 2.3 million kuna from more than 11 on Tuesday.
The biggest gainer was Karlovacka Pivovara brewery, rising 15 kuna to 240 on a volume of 109 units.

Fully listed Zagrebacka Banka rose for the third straight day, adding 13 kuna to its all-time high of 1,913 kuna on a small volume of 210 shares. It has gained more than 10 percent since last Thursday.
"One should expect its price to grow futher," said Milisa, referring to a combination of good news about the bank's business activities including a forthcoming credit rating.
Zagrebacka's E-series preference stock gained 10 kuna to 1,080 with 80 shares sold.
Another blue chip, drugs firm Pliva, slid six kuna to 464 with 317 shares sold. But its stocks are likely to rise, boosted by expectations of good results for 1996, Milisa said.

All five liquid hoteliers' shares were flat or recorded losses on small volumes. Traders said their prices have now reached the bottom and would not slide further ahead of another good tourist season.
Wednesday's leading decliner was Dalmatinska Banka which lost 70 kuna to 390 selling 50 shares.
